findings.failureScenario: UiState mixes saved preferences with per-frame transient state, separated only by per-field #[serde(skip)]. renaming_component (an inline mask-component rename in progress) lacks the skip that its sibling renaming_mask (state.rs:621-622) has, so it is serialized. PrefsWriter::save_ui writes ui.json whenever the serialized state changes (main.rs:332-350), so starting a rename writes Some((mask_id, index, text)) to disk, and sanitized() (1209-1226) does not clear it. After a quit or crash mid-rename, the next launch restores it. masking.rs:309-315 then shows a rename field on any photo with a mask of that id and component index, and request_focus() on every frame takes keyboard focus away from other widgets until the user presses Esc or leaves the field. The stale text is also exposed through ui.get.
findings.action: Mark renaming_component #[serde(skip)] like renaming_mask, or reset it in sanitized(). Consider splitting UiState's transient fields into a non-serialized struct so new transient fields can't be persisted by mistake.

anchor.text: return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("unknown or duplicate favorite theme"));

findings.failureScenario: favorite_themes uses a validating deserializer that returns an error for any unknown or duplicate theme id. An error in one field fails deserialization of the whole UiState. decode_saved_ui recovers only the docking field (main.rs:226-240), so load_prefs_at treats the whole ui.json as damaged: the file is renamed to ui.json.corrupt-* and every setting reverts to defaults, including library path, keymap, panel layout and appearance (main.rs:263-279). This happens when a ui.json written by a build with an extra or renamed theme id is opened by another build (downgrade, web vs native, or a theme removed later), or when the file is hand-edited. That is the opposite of the persistence policy the same file follows for the keymap, where a bad entry is ignored (shortcuts.rs:54-57).
findings.action: Make the field tolerant: deserialize Vec<String>, then drop unknown ids and duplicates (as the keymap does) instead of returning an error. Keep strict validation for the control-channel write path if that is where it is wanted.

findings.failureScenario: Each Dialog variant is defined in state.rs (780-1018), but its behaviour is spread over separate exhaustive or partial matches in dialogs.rs: title (223-265), width (289-293), body (299-1120, inside the 1,143-line show() function), confirm_dialog (1571-1751), return_confirms (1946-1948), window_id (176-182) and keeps_open (1416-1418). Some dialogs delegate their body to their own module (Merge, Import, Settings, Sync, Denoise, Faces). Export instead renders 327 lines inline in one match arm (660-987). The partial matches (return_confirms, window_id, keeps_open, width) fall through silently, so a new dialog that needs Return-to-confirm, its own window id, or a stay-open rule compiles without them. The scattering already shows in the confirm_dialog doc comment, which has drifted onto fmt_gap (1400-1402).
findings.action: Move large inline bodies (Export, KeywordTag, KeywordSet, CaptureTime) into their own functions or modules, like Merge, Import and Settings. Consider gathering per-dialog metadata (title, width, window id, Return-confirms, keeps-open) into one method on Dialog, so adding a variant takes one exhaustive match instead of several partial ones.
